analyst.summary: Zydus had a strong FY26 on paper -- revenue up 17%, profit up 11-15%, margins expanding -- but a large part of the growth engine behind that print, generic Revlimid and generic Myrbetriq (mirabegron), is now winding down or capped by a licensing deadline in September 2027, so the reported growth rate overstates what the ongoing business can repeat. The stock, near its 52-week high at roughly 21-22 times trailing earnings, is priced about in line with the sector already, and several sell-side price targets sit below today's quote. The India branded-medicines business remains a genuine, well-run compounder, and a possible new US specialty drug (Saroglitazar, under FDA priority review with a decision due late November 2026) offers real upside if approved -- but two separate, unresolved US FDA plant matters surfaced in 2026 (a 7-observation inspection at a biologics injectable site, and a warning letter at a formulation plant over an excipient specification) add near-term regulatory uncertainty. On balance this reads as a Hold: a quality franchise that looks fully valued for now, not a name to add to or exit in a hurry.
